text:
The chuppah is a beautiful and central tradition in Jewish weddings. It’s a canopy under which the couple stands during the ceremony, symbolizing the home they will build together. The open sides represent hospitality and inclusion, welcoming family and friends into their lives. Traditionally, it’s supported by four poles and can be as simple as a tallit (prayer shawl) or as elaborate as a decorated fabric.

The chuppah is often held by friends or family members, adding a personal touch, though it can also be freestanding. It’s typically placed outdoors or under the open sky to symbolize divine blessings, though indoor settings are also common today.
